titulo: Assessing the class: rubric, practical test, internal champions and follow-up
lead: "I really liked it" on a satisfaction survey doesn't prove anyone learned. You need to see the person doing the work, against a clear standard, and come back weeks later to see whether the habit stuck. This lesson covers the 4-level rubric, the practical test, how to choose the internal champion, and the 30-, 60- and 90-day follow-up plan.
objetivo: assess the class with a 4-level rubric and a practical test, choose the internal champion and set up the 90-day follow-up.

aprende.t: The 4 levels of evaluating a training
A 4-level rubric for the delegate, review, approve cycle
Who the internal champion is (and who they are not)
The follow-up ritual that makes the habit stick

hero_alt: Evaluation sheets with a four-column grid on the table and, in the background, people talking in pairs.

secoes.titulo: What to measure, from easiest to what matters
secoes.sub: The 4 levels of the Kirkpatrick model. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: A survey at the end of class. Useful for adjusting pace and examples, but it doesn't prove learning. Also ask: "what will you do differently next week?".
A hands-on test at the end of the workshop: one real task, with a planted output to review, scored by the rubric. Watching someone do it is worth more than asking if they understood.

nos.sub: do they use it at work?
nos.detalhe: Weeks later, is the person using the cycle at work? Count it in the usage log and the weekly check-ins. This is where training usually dies, and where the internal champion makes a difference.

Did the number agreed on in the proposal (lesson 2) change? Response time, complaints resolved the same day, rework. Compare it with the number from before; without a baseline, there is no result to show (failure F11).

secoes.legenda: Almost all training measures only reaction. Yours measures at least learning and behavior.
secoes.dica: Agree on the level 4 number before the workshop. Afterward, no one remembers what it was.

secoes.sub: Three pieces that turn a class into a habit.

texto: One task from the area: delegate a request, review an output with 3 planted errors and decide 3 actions (go ahead, approve, block). Same as the lesson 4 exercises, with a new case.
Score it with the rubric and give back the level with one sentence of feedback. A score without feedback doesn't teach.

exemplo.texto: Level 3 review: you found all 3 errors. To reach level 4, write the rule that would have prevented the wrong discount.

passos.sub: a person's name, not a job title
texto: This is the person who watches usage every day, gathers questions and brings them to the weekly check-in. A good champion: has been at the company for over a year, has time set aside on their calendar, wants the role (their own words) and has the authority to make adjustments.
The wrong champion: someone who will leave in a few months, someone who already has too many duties, someone who was assigned without being asked.

exemplo.texto: Juliana uses the agent and the summaries every day: she's a natural candidate, if she wants the role and has time on her calendar. Or a senior attendant who scored level 3 or 4 on the test.

texto: Same day and time every week. Fixed agenda: the week's numbers, questions from the log, one improvement and the next date.
A question that comes up 3 times becomes a 3-to-4-minute microvideo or a line in the 1-page guide.

exemplo.texto: 5 min numbers · 10 min questions and adjustments · 5 min next week.

texto: Day 30: behavior (how many people use the cycle and how often). Day 60: a second short hands-on test, to see who moved up a level. Day 90: results against the number from before and a decision on the next step.
Recognize in public the people who brought results: people imitate what they see being valued.

exemplo.texto: Keep it, expand it to another area, or fix what didn't stick.

secoes.sub: The rubric and the plan go in the lesson 8 kit.

blocos.conteudo:
RUBRIC · <class> · <date>
Levels: 1 Beginner · 2 Developing · 3 Proficient · 4 Reference

DELEGATE
1 vague request ("make a summary")
2 states the result, but with no context or format
3 result + context + format + what is off limits
4 level 3 + asks for proof (cite the source) and reuses it as a template

REVIEW
1 doesn't review, or only fixes grammar
2 finds 1 of the 3 planted errors
3 finds all 3 errors (fact, rule, personal data)
4 level 3 + writes the rule that prevents the error next time

APPROVE AND SECURITY
1 lets an irreversible action go out without approval
2 recognizes the high value, but not the injection or the personal data
3 classifies all 3 actions correctly (go ahead / approve / block)
4 level 3 + says who approves and what to record

APPLY AT WORK (day 30)
1 didn't use it
2 used it 1 or 2 times
3 uses it every week on the agreed task
4 uses it and taught a colleague or created a template for the team

Class goal: most people at level 3 in delegate and review on exam day.

FOLLOW-UP · <company> · <area> · start <date>

INTERNAL CHAMPION
- Name: <...> · time at the company: <...> · time in their schedule: <30 min/day>
- Accepted the role in their own words? ( ) yes
- Backup if they leave: <name>

WEEKLY CHECK-IN · <fixed day and time> · 15-20 min
- 0-5 numbers · 5-15 questions from the log · 15-20 next week

USE AND QUESTIONS LOG (1 tab)
date | person | task | what the AI got wrong | what we did
- A question that comes up 3 times becomes a micro-video (3-4 min) or a line in the guide

INDICATORS (4 at most)
1. People using the cycle this week: <n of n>
2. Cases done with AI and review: <n>
3. Errors found in review: <n> (a rise at the start is a good sign)
4. Agreed result number: before <...> · now <...>

MILESTONES
- Day 30: behavior ("apply" rubric)
- Day 60: short practical exam
- Day 90: result vs. before · decision: keep / expand / fix

secoes.sub: Both pieces go into the lesson 8 kit.

exercicios.texto: Adapt the rubric to the area you chose in lesson 5: replace the examples at each level with situations from that area.
exercicios.pronto: each criterion has 4 levels described by something you can observe, with no words like "good" or "satisfactory".

exercicios.texto: Fill in the 90-day plan with a champion (real or from Horizonte), the day and time of the check-in, and the indicators.
exercicios.pronto: the plan has a champion with a backup, a check-in with a day and time, 4 indicators at most, and the 3 milestones with dates.

secoes.sub: 4 questions. The explanation appears after your attempt.

perguntas.p: The survey at the end of the workshop scored 9.5. What does that prove?
opcoes: That the class liked it; learning shows in the practical exam and in habit, weeks later
That the company's results will improve
perguntas.explica: Reaction is level 1. Liking it is a good sign, but it doesn't show whether people can do it or will use it.

perguntas.p: On the exam, the person found 2 of the 3 planted errors. Which review level is that?
perguntas.explica: Level 3 requires all 3 errors. Give the level back with one sentence: which error got through and how to find it.

perguntas.p: Who is the best internal champion?
opcoes: The intern who is good with computers and leaves in 3 months
The senior support agent, with set-aside time, who wants the role and scored level 3 on the exam
Whoever the owner picked without asking
perguntas.explica: A champion must stay, have time in their schedule, and want the role. A champion who leaves takes the knowledge with them, and the project is left orphaned.

perguntas.p: The same question showed up 3 times in the log. What should you do?
opcoes: Turn it into a short micro-video or a line in the 1-page guide
perguntas.explica: A repeated question is material. Answering one by one doesn't scale; the micro-video answers everyone.

itens.texto: Reaction, learning, behavior, and result. Measure at least the middle ones.
Delegate, review, approve, and apply, with observable descriptions.
A real name, time in their schedule, willingness stated in their own words, a backup defined.
A fixed weekly check-in and milestones at 30, 60, and 90 days.
